BAGONG PLIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. JUN 1 1 2025 MARIBETH D. SERVANO Federation President Federation of Solo Parents Mandaue City Chapter Zone 2 Upper Brgy. Canduman Mandaue City Fspmc2023@gmail.com Dear Ms. Servano: This has reference to your Letter dated November 18, 2024, addressed to the DILG City Director of Mandaue City, which was subsequently referred to this Level for guidance, relative to your request for clarification on item (ii) of 5.5 (Criteria for Assistance) under DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2023-1401, which provides that: "5.5 Criteria for Assistance Eligible for assistance shall be a solo parent that (i) xxx: and (iii is not a recipient of any other subsidy from other qovernment proqrams, provided that senior citizens and persons with disability (PWD) may continue to receiving their corresponding benefits without forfeiting benefits under RA 11861. Xxx" It is intimated that Mandaue City has enacted its Solo Parent Ordinance pursuant to Republic Act (RA) No. 11861, otherwise known as the "Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act." Said ordinance is set to extend financial assistance for solo parents. Ostensibly, the majority of solo parents registered and qualified to receive the cash subsidy under the said ordinance opted not to be a beneficiary of the Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/DispIaced Workers (TUPAD) and the Ayuda sa Kapos ang Kita Program (AKAP) on the apprehension that their eligibility for assistance under RA 11861 would be forfeited in light of the aforementioned DILG MC in question. Hence, your request for this Department's clarification on the interpretation of "not a recipient of anv other subsidy from other qovemment proqrams." and whether TUPAD and AKAP are considered subsidy programs of the government. 1 "Guidelines for Local Govemment Units and other Concemed on the Implementation of RA 11861, Otherwise Knowns as the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Acts. " "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Foremost, may we note that the subject DILG MC was issued to provide guidance to local government units (LGUs) in the implementation of RA 11861. It is worth noting that the provision under Item 5.5 of DILG MC in question is consistent with Section 12 of RA 11861 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR). Section 12(a) of RA 11861 reads: "Section 12. xxx (a) Means-, pension-, and subsidy-tested monthly cash subsidy of One thousand pesos (Pl ,OOO.OO) per month per solo parent who is earning a minimum wage and below, to be allocated by the concerned city or municipal govenrment in accordance with Section 17(b)(2)(iv) of the Local Government Code: Provided, That for fifth (5th) class municipalities and lower, as well as the five hundred (500) municipalities with the highest poverty incidence based on the latest municipal-level small area poverty estimates, cash subsidy allocations may be taken from the Gender and Development (GAD) budget and the amount of cash subsidy per recipient may be dependent on the amount of the GAD budget: Provided. further. That the solo parent under this section is not a recipient of any other cash assistance or subsidy from any other govemment programs: Provided, finally, That a beneficiary who is also a senior citizen or a person with disability (PWD) may continue receiving senior citizen or PWD benefits without forfeiting the benefits under this Act" (Emphasis ours) Here, it is equally worth noting that the afore-cited provision uses the phrase "any other govemment programs" without distinction between long-term programs or short-term government programs. Neither RA 11861 nor its IRR clearly delineate the scope of "any other govemment programs." On the contrary, the wording of the provision encompasses all govemment programs, regardless of the program's nature. It is an elementary rule in statutory construction that where the law does not distinguish, neither should we. Ubi lex non distinguit, nec nos distinguere debemus. Accordingly, there should be no distinction in the application of a law where none is indicated. As the Supreme Court has consistently reiterated, where the law is free from ambiguity, the court may not introduce exceptions or conditions where none is provided from considerations of convenience, public welfare, or for any laudable purpose; neither may it engraft into the law qualifications not contemplated.2 Premised on the foregoing, this Department opines that solo parents who are recipients of the financial subsidy under Section 12 of the Solo Parents Act must not be recipients of other government programs, such as TUPAD and AKAP, which are both govemment programs. The law is clear that only the senior citizens and persons with disabilities may continue receiving their respective benefits without forfeiture. 2 Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board v. Central Mindanao Construction Multi-Purpose Cooperative [G.R. No. 242296, July 31, 20241. Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs ANNA LIZA F. BONAGUA, CESO 111 Director. BLGD LEOCADIO T.
